body:
Thank you for this issue.
Definitely appreciate PRs!

I opened an issue on espree before I merged #5512 : https://github.com/eslint/espree/issues/256
I think this fixing needs 2 steps.
1. Fixes the bug on espree.
2. Adds tests for the bug on eslint.

PR opened for the Espree change. Will get to adding the tests on ESLint after that lands :+1:

https://github.com/eslint/espree/pull/257

My fix was merged and it looks like @nzakas released a new version of espree. Would the next step be for me to open a PR that bumps the version of espree in this repo and add tests that assert the fixed `getComment` behavior? Thanks for your help with this.

@kaicataldo Espree versions are not locked in ESLint. So just doing `npm install` would get you the new version of Espree. However, if the change that you are planning on doing in ESLint would not work with previous version of Espree, then you should up the version in package.json.
@ilyavolodin Thanks! I'll try to get a PR together in the next day or two

I've discovered that the changes I made to espree don't fully cover what we need. My change runs under the assumption that the `body` property is always an array, which I'm finding is incorrect. Looks like we might have to look recursively in each `body` and also change the check depending on if `body` is an array or an object. I can open another issue on espree and am currently working on this.

Edit: Alternately, I can just reference the already closed espree issue since it's really more work on the same accepted issue.

Made another PR with fixes here: https://github.com/eslint/espree/pull/262 Would love some eyes on it to see if this makes sense. Thanks all! When the espree issue is fixed I'll finish up my PR to close this issue.

rename.from: Leading tokens incorrectly include comments inside previous token
rename.to: Leading comments incorrectly include comments inside previous token

body: Hey @scottohara, thanks for letting us know! Can you file a new issue for this? There's a good chance this is caused by the same bug, but it may also be a problem with one of the rules you mentioned. A new issue will help us triage this better.
